open_points.subject: OWNER_FORM_FIELDS name uniqueness
open_points.text: No two rows share a name: the name alone picks a row, and a table in which two rows share one is not a release.
open_points.question: Which module or release-validation tool owns and enforces this uniqueness rule, given that `models` must not own any check and `data_provider` must not own validation?
options: The specification/release validator rejects duplicate names before code generation.
The `data_provider` module validates the table when the release starts.
Each consumer detects duplicate names when constructing its lookup.
open_points.default_guess: Make the specification/release validator enforce uniqueness before code generation.

witness.initial: A proposed release contains two OWNER_FORM_FIELDS rows with the same name and different carriers or value kinds.
events: The release author submits the proposed data closure for assembly.
A careful implementer assigns the check to release validation; another assigns it to generated runtime code because no owner is named.
outcomes: Assembly rejects the proposed release before generating or starting Registry.
Assembly succeeds, but Registry or an owner-interface consumer rejects the table when it builds the lookup.
witness.observer: The release author sees the failure at a different phase and cannot know which component must implement or test the rule.
